## Design

### 2026-10-23 – Turns out I bit off a lot more than I could chew (who could've guessed?).

**2h**

Turns out I bit off a lot more than I could chew (who could've guessed?).
The original idea reel I made planned for the following components:
- 1x Waveshare ESP32-S3-Zero
- 4x Kailh Choc Low-Profile Switches
- 8x EC11 Rotary Encoders
- 2x Bourns Slide Potentiometers
- 12x Capacitive Touchpads

This was the approximate layout I had made:
![Old layout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/a8d18bf916e22c233e29336c7d50525044fe97d94066a98410b07d49357c5b07.png)
Adding it up, all the components need **43** GPIO pins on the microcontroller. For context, the microcontroller I'm using (which I specifically chose so I'd have more GPIO) has 15 (usable) pins.

So, after a ton of research, reading datasheets, and counting pins, I scaled back my plan a bunch so I could still have a final outcome similar to what I wanted while keeping it actually practical. This is what the new, much more modest, approximate layout looks like:

![New layout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/e7af2144fcf0b7ffa6ea7fdd935a0672542c848a714011f1cc67de03a2654b7d.png)

As you can see, the new design has:
- The same microcontroller
- The same number of touchpads
- 1 less key switch
- 1 less potentiometer
- 6 less rotary encoders

Most of the pin saving comes from the huge decrease in rotary encoders (those use 2 pins each, 3 if you want the switch functionality, which I do) and that extra chip you may have noticed.

That chip is a breakout board for the MPR121. While digging for methods to reduce my GPIO count, I stumbled across a discontinued chip that claims to serve the input of 12 capacitive pads over I2C (how convenient, that's exactly how many I need). The I2C connection only needs 4 pins (IRQ, SCL, SDA, and ADD), so all 12 pads can be hooked up to the microcontroller with only those 4 pins.

The actual MPR121 is a tiny 3mmx3mm QFN chip. That's why I need a breakout board to actually use it. The chip itself is technically discontinued, but there's still two main sources from which I can choose to buy the board.
- Adafruit makes a breakout board for the MPR121. It's well documented, easy to design around, and even has a bunch of QoL features like an LED indicator and a 3V regulator.
- There's also a generic-brand breakout board for the chip. It isn't well documented, and doesn't have most of the Adafruit board's benefits. *Except*, it's like 7 times cheaper.

I decided on the latter. This meant I had to make my own KiCAD symbol and footprint for the board and set it up in a library. Thankfully, I have some experience doing that and I was able to without much hassle. Hopefully this isn't foreshadowing.

That brings the total number of GPIO needed by my design down to exactly 15. Perfect. Now I'll begin designing the schematic for the board (my second favourite step!)

### 2026-10-23 – I created the schematic for the board in KiCad. While examining the pins on the MPR121 board, I realised I can actually save a GPIO pin by not wiring the ADD (address) pin. The pin is only needed if t

**1.52h**

I created the schematic for the board in KiCad. While examining the pins on the MPR121 board, I realised I can actually save a GPIO pin by not wiring the ADD (address) pin. The pin is only needed if the microcontroller is managing multiple I2C connections with the same SDA and SCL pins and the board I'm using already has a jumper tying the pin to GND, so it won't be floating. This meant I had one extra GPIO pin which I used to add another key switch to make it 4 in a grid (like the original plan). This also meant 4 LEDs instead of 3, one for each switch. Here is what the final schematic looks like:
![Schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/2411edecbc1ffe73718614324370a5798971be996fdffc09c49c47d1a4c0468f.png)

I also designed the footprint for the capacitive pads. An octave worth of piano keys. Each white key is 20mm wide and each black key is 10mm wide. The minimum gap between adjacent pads is 2mm.

![Footprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/6717c060e22fef928f4f3696f8b4e44ae7066f4c560f549d60e85ffdd0d8c718.png)
